model: Mannheim--O'Brien thin exponential-disk conformal-gravity rotation model

published_model_source.citation: P. D. Mannheim and J. G. O'Brien, Fitting galactic rotation curves with conformal gravity and a global quadratic potential, Phys. Rev. D 85 (2012) 124020

independent_observation_source.citation: F. Lelli, S. S. McGaugh, and J. M. Schombert, SPARC: Mass Models for 175 Disk Galaxies with Spitzer Photometry and Accurate Rotation Curves, Astron. J. 152 (2016) 157
independent_observation_source.selection: All 43 rows whose fixed-width ID field is NGC3198, copied without numerical alteration

published_modelling_assumptions.gas_geometry: infinitesimally thin exponential disk with scale length four times the optical scale length
published_modelling_assumptions.free_parameter: stellar mass-to-blue-light ratio; the table reports the fitted value 1.12
published_modelling_assumptions.universal_parameters: beta_star, gamma_star, gamma_0, and kappa are held fixed at the published values

cross_dataset_protocol.radius_rescaling: Multiply each SPARC radius by 14.1/13.8 to use the distance adopted in the published conformal-gravity fit
cross_dataset_protocol.comparison_window: Rescaled radius less than or equal to the published last radius 38.6 kpc
cross_dataset_protocol.uncertainty: SPARC e_Vobs random errors only; inclination and other systematic uncertainties are not included

does_not_establish: identity of the SPARC 2016 photometric reduction with the heterogeneous data and blue-band photometry used in the 2012 fit
reproduction of the original fitting algorithm, likelihood, covariance model, or full 111-galaxy analysis
that the fitted mass-to-light ratio is independently preferred by the SPARC data
that the matter-coupling and conformal-frame assumptions required for massive bodies to follow the displayed metric are physically correct
